chunks: And from him, from Al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), that a Prophet from the Prophets complained to his Lord, saying: 'O Lord! How can I judge regarding what I did not witness and did not see?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'Judge between them by My Book, and add them to My Name, so make them swear by it.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is for the one for whom a clear proof cannot be established.'
ai.seo_question: How does Islamic jurisprudence handle cases where there is no clear evidence or proof?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, establishes the prophetic precedent for using oaths (yamin) as a legal proof in the absence of definitive evidence (bayyinah), linking judicial authority directly to divine revelation. It highlights the methodological principle in Shia jurisprudence that when factual certainty is lacking, the court relies on the sworn testimony of the parties, attributing their claim to God to ensure truthfulness. This mechanism serves as a critical bridge between divine guidance and practical adjudication in Islamic courts.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman, Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘In the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, a Prophet<sup>as</sup> from the Prophets<sup>as</sup> complained to his<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, so he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! How can I<sup>as</sup> judge with regards to what I<sup>as</sup> did not witness and did not see?’ So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “Judge between them by My<sup>azwj</sup> Book, and add them to My<sup>azwj</sup> Name, so get them to swear by it’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is for the one for him the proof cannot be established’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said

that it is in the book of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that one of the Prophets complained before his Lord saying, ‘O Lord, how can I judge among people what I have not witnessed?’ Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, then sent him revelation that said, ‘Judge among them by means of my book and making them to swear by My name.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘This is in the case of those who cannot establish evidence and testimony.’”
